facts.subject: 9-5 5D rear cargo floor
facts.notes: Factory assembly/repair topology not a claim that all those areas are rusty.

facts.subject: 9-5 5D rear cargo floor
facts.notes: 50 mm is a section repair cut placement in manufacturer's procedure, NOT an acceptable corrosion depth or a DIY measure.

facts.subject: 9-5 5D rear cargo floor
facts.value: If original joint is MIG brazed, conventional welding/filler is prohibited: restore MIG brazing for crash performance.
facts.notes: Professional structural repair boundary. Do not tell a buyer to weld underbody patches using an ordinary welder.

facts.subject: 9-5 rear subframe-to-body captive nut

value.access: interior floor through designated marked opening

facts.notes: This is a repair for a captive nut, not a procedure that permits rust-thinned adjacent load-bearing metal or makes a subframe bolt safe to torque in rotten floor.

facts.subject: 9-5 rear frame member
facts.value: Only cut/join behind illustrated marking; if damaged farther forward renew complete frame member and measure alignment.
facts.notes: No numeric rust depth or universally acceptable sectioning location is established without the original illustration.

facts.subject: 9-5 5D C-pillar and side panel
facts.value: Partial side-panel procedure warns cutting outside factory point risks damaging inner C-pillar reinforcement; restore MIG brazing where present.
facts.notes: Side/rear wheelhouse or sill corrosion beneath visible skin requires reinforcement evaluation; not proof of frequent rust.

facts.subject: 9-5 rear suspension mounting

value.service: subframe lowered one side to press out/in bushing
value.safety: tighten some transverse link joints at ground ride height

facts.notes: Bushing repairable does not imply rear subframe or body anchor corrosion safely repairable or same assembly across years.

facts.subject: 9-5 lifting positions

value.front: front subframe at front towing-eye mounting
value.rear: rear towing eye or towbar mount

facts.notes: Only when lift points themselves are intact; never assume corroded jack pad can carry a car.

facts.subject: 9-5 lifting positions
facts.notes: Avoid undercar access beneath a vehicle with uncertain support structure; use an inspected professional lift.

facts.subject: 9-5 petrol fuel system

relationships: rear exhaust removed for tank service

facts.notes: Inspection map for lines, clips, shields, straps, leaks around body rear underfloor, not permission to lower a rusted tank at home.

facts.subject: 9-5 petrol fuel system
facts.value: Saab requires new rubber hoses between filler and tank on refit because repeat clip tightening can cause cracking and fuel leaks.
facts.notes: Only when actually performing documented tank removal. Do not infer fuel-line replacement needed without damage.

facts.subject: 9-3 rear subframe 2006
facts.notes: A rusted subframe repair budget needs adjacent safety-line/harness inspection; NOT proof that these parts are already defective.

facts.subject: 9-3 rear subframe 2006
facts.value: CV only: rear chassis reinforcement is removed/refitted as part of rear subframe service; sedan/5D no such step in this procedure.
facts.notes: Convertible structural complexity differs, so donor rear suspension/repair scope must be verified per body.

facts.subject: 9-3 convertible structural sill
facts.value: Factory inner sill replacement involves aligning bench, outer front sill, centre sill, side panel, spot/plug welding and cavity treatment.
facts.notes: Rust in structural convertible sill is not a simple cosmetic patch or an automatic acceptable first DIY welding job.

facts.subject: 9-3 B207 fuel tank and pipes
facts.value: Inspect under car AND engine bay: fuel tank, lines, quick-release couplings for damage/leaks, and secure line mounts.
facts.notes: Factory does not give a universal allowable fuel-line corrosion thickness; damage/leaks/sagging lines require a safe qualified assessment.

facts.subject: 9-3 B207 fuel/underbody pipe routing
facts.value: To replace fuel lines, the factory lowers rear of front subframe and unclips fuel lines and nearby brake pipes from holders; warns against brake pipe damage.
facts.notes: This is a direct reason to examine mounting clips and adjacent lines when inspecting rusted subframes; not routine DIY permission to lower frame.

facts.subject: NYS passenger vehicle inspection

look_for: severe rust at suspension attachment points
value.applies: cars and light trucks in NY

facts.locator: Safety items: Steering Front End Suspension Chassis Frame
facts.notes: Legal-state specific screening criteria, not a manufacturer source for numeric Saab body corrosion threshold; station inspection decides compliance.

facts.subject: NYS passenger vehicle inspection

value.fuel: any leak causing dripping or pooling unacceptable

facts.locator: Safety items: Brakes and Fuel Leaks
facts.notes: Does not mean a no-drip line with severe corrosion or structurally loose clip is safe.

facts.subject: NYS passenger vehicle inspection

value.repairs: may repair elsewhere or yourself but must pass before inspection sticker

facts.notes: Car must also be safe whenever driven; annual inspection alone is not future structural soundness warranty.

facts.subject: 9-5 front subframe MY2006 petrol
facts.notes: The removed frame supports multiple systems; inspect adjacent body rails and line mounts before pricing a replacement.

facts.subject: 9-3 convertible centre sill
facts.value: Factory replacement requires alignment/cross measurement if necessary, removal of adjoining panels, controlled spot/plug welding, primer, seam sealing and cavity protection.
facts.notes: Do not treat under-plastic outer sill appearance as a structural safety verdict.

issues.title: Original 9-5 SportCombi rear subframe rust requires mounting-metal and rear-floor inspection
issues.cause: WIS separately documents body captive nuts, rear frame member section boundaries, welded wagon rear floor/reinforcement, and suspension subframe bushes; these are mechanically distinct repair paths.
symptoms: rear subframe visibly rusted or reported unsafe
flaking around rear suspension fasteners or body captive-nut mount
corrosion in wagon rear wheelhouse/rear-floor seams
issues.diagnosis_summary: On a known-safe professional lift, separately inspect rear subframe tube/arms, bushes, captive nut seats and surrounding floor, rear frame members, sill/wheelhouse, brake and fuel pipes, with photos and shop assessment of sectioning/geometry if suspect.
issues.correction_summary: Replace only verified serviceable bolt-on components when structurally sound body anchors are confirmed. Escalate thinning/cracks near frame members or suspension mounts for qualified structural estimate; unknown mount integrity blocks purchase-safety clearance.
limits: MY2006 factory procedure is NOT independently proven to cover the exact MY2008 wagon in question.
No numeric Saab rust-depth rejection threshold or failure frequency.
A repair procedure is not evidence it is inexpensive, safe with weakened body metal, or straightforward DIY.

issues.title: NG9-3 convertible hidden sill and rear subframe require different structural approach
issues.cause: Convertible sill/floor reinforcements and a rear chassis reinforcement require structural alignment and special joining; rear subframe service touches multiple safety systems.
symptoms: soft/jacked sill or damage under sill cover
rust around rear frame mounting bushes
issues.diagnosis_summary: Record photos of the inner/centre/outer sill and junctions, roofless chassis reinforcements, rear subframe body bolts, adjacent lines and lifting integrity; qualified body inspection is needed for any suspected load-bearing loss.
issues.correction_summary: Factory describes complex structural repairs, but approval to repair depends on confirmed material/geometry and capable specialist. Do not use sedan reinforcement plan or cosmetic patch as substitute.
limits: MY2006 CV procedures not an all-year 9440 collision-repair blanket approval.
No penetrative inspection, thickness measurement, repair quote or car photos reviewed.

issues.title: Brake/fuel pipe and chassis corrosion is an independent no-drive screening condition in NY
issues.cause: NYS DMV examines chassis/frame cracks and severe rust at suspension attachment points, brake lines for leaks/chafing/support, and fuel leaks causing drips/pooling. WIS shows fuel/handbrake/exhaust routing near subframes.
symptoms: brake lines cracked, chafed or unsupported
severe rust or cracking at suspension pickup
issues.diagnosis_summary: Without driving or unsafe lifting, document visible indications; have a certified NYS inspection station or suitable specialist evaluate suspension attachment metal and brake/fuel routing. Stop if any leak or severe structural question remains.
issues.correction_summary: Repair proven hydraulic/fuel/structural defects to applicable factory procedures; re-inspect. Do not issue an inspection pass, legal guarantee or structural thickness approval from photos alone.
limits: NYS page describes minimum inspection checklist, not a complete vehicle engineering study.
A car might pass minimum inspection yet have costly corrosion outside the limited zones.
No observed vehicle data or measured leakage.
